definitions.explanation: books or records used to keep track of financial transactions

examples.japanese: {税務署|ぜいむしょ}の{調査|ちょうさ}のために{帳簿|ちょうぼ}を{整理|せいり}した。
examples.english: I organized the financial records for the tax office audit.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}の{売上|うりあげ}を{帳簿|ちょうぼ}に{記録|きろく}することが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to record daily sales in the ledger.

notes:
{帳簿|ちょうぼ} refers to financial record books used for accounting purposes.

WRITING:
- {帳|ちょう} (notebook, register)
- {簿|ぼ} (register, record book)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {帳簿|ちょうぼ}をつける (to keep books)
- {帳簿|ちょうぼ}を{記入|きにゅう}する (to make entries in the ledger)
- {帳簿|ちょうぼ}を{確認|かくにん}する (to check the records)
- {帳簿|ちょうぼ}{管理|かんり} (bookkeeping)

TYPES OF {帳簿|ちょうぼ}:
- {現金|げんきん}{出納帳|すいとうちょう} (cash book)
- {売上帳|うりあげちょう} (sales ledger)
- {仕入帳|しいれちょう} (purchase ledger)
- {総勘定元帳|そうかんじょうもとちょう} (general ledger)

LEGAL REQUIREMENT:
- Businesses are legally required to maintain {帳簿|ちょうぼ} for tax purposes
- Must be kept for a certain number of years
